newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Occidental sets force majeure in cano Limon field.
newsitem.headline: Occidental sets force majeure in cano Limon field.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp shut in production and declared force majeure in the Cano Limon field it operates in northeast Colombia Monday for the second time in three weeks, a company spokesman said.

The move comes in the wake of two leftist rebel dynamite attacks and a landslide over the weekend, which partially destroyed the pipeline that pumps crude to the Caribbean coast lifting terminal at Covenas.
"Given the events that we are all now aware of we are going ahead and declaring force majeure (in our Cano Limon field)," an Occidental spokesman said.

He added that production at the field, which produces an average 175,000 barrels per day, was shut in earlier Monday. The pipeline, the second largest in the country with a 250,000 barrels per day capacity, has been out of operation since last Wednesday after an earlier rebel dynamite attack.

Occidental has capacity to store only about three days production on-site at Cano Limon. Earlier Monday the state-run oil company Ecopetrol said it would take about four or five days to repair the pipeline and declared force majeure on the transport of crude. No decision has yet been made on liftings and exports of crude from Covenas.

Occidental last declared force majeure -- which effectively allows it to temporarily suspend contracts with contractors and most of its own staff -- in the field on July 15 in the wake of back-to-back rebel attacks. That situation lasted four days.
